final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence. The response mainly narrows and caveats the claim, and that clarification is directionally more careful, but it does not cure the core compliance failure. The governing record still shows a material weakness affecting a named launch use case tied to customer commitments, an open legal review on disclosure, and no admissible proof of any policy-safe condition: resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, a caveated certification defense may describe a business posture, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat itself is the unresolved compliance predicate. This is therefore a reinterpretation of the same evidence, not a change driven by new admissible facts.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still shows a 1.4 percentage point miss in the supply-chain vendor screening segment.
That segment is named in two manufacturer rollout commitments, so it remains material under the stated policy.
There is still no admissible evidence that the gap was resolved before launch.
There is still no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this exact gap before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, leaving the policy predicate unresolved at decision time.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness but do not satisfy the specific release-policy condition for a material named-segment limitation.
